assigned.title: Artwork, end to end, because a media application without images is a list
assigned.acceptance: Titles have artwork, and getting it does not become a new way to fetch arbitrary URLs. ACCEPTANCE RECONCILED IN ROUND 83 ON gpt-architect's RULING. The previous wording asked for a rights basis and dimensions 'beside the URL'. The repository already has a reviewed artwork vocabulary that deliberately carries NO URL: artworkRefSchema in packages/catalog-ingestion/src/record.ts holds a role, an assetRef constrained to an opaque lower-case token, and a REQUIRED rights basis -- required there and nowhere else in that package, on the stated argument that a work with an undeclared basis is merely refused from browse while an IMAGE with an undeclared basis that reached a page would be somebody else's file served from our origin. project.ts then drops artwork on the way to CatalogItem, and domains/catalog.ts opens by promising the browse shape carries no stream, URL or provider field. The ruling is explicit: do not weaken a previously rights- and security-reviewed opaque-reference boundary to satisfy stale task prose. REQUIRED: the catalog and title contracts carry an OPAQUE ARTWORK REFERENCE plus required display metadata and a rights basis. Not a URL. The vocabulary ADOPTS artworkRefSchema's shape rather than inventing a second one; where the two must differ, say why in the module. REQUIRED: the client never receives an arbitrary upstream image URL merely to render artwork. REQUIRED: an authorized artwork-resolution boundary turns the opaque reference into a fetchable or served asset under allowlisted transport policy. That boundary is where an origin is decided, and it is the only place one is. REQUIRED: no arbitrary URL proxy. SECURITY.md's 'never proxy arbitrary client-provided URLs' is not weakened for pictures, which is why this task carries a security review as well as a rights review. REQUIRED: absent artwork keeps the DESIGNED gradient fallback. An absent image is a designed state, not a broken one, and a broken-image icon is not the answer. REQUIRED: next/image -- or whatever equivalent configuration the implementation uses -- permits only the controlled Liberty artwork origin or boundary, never arbitrary remote hosts and never a wildcard. Because no other origin is expressible through the resolution boundary, this should be a structural fact rather than a check somebody has to remember to maintain; state which of the two the implementation achieves. MEASURED STARTING POINT, unchanged and still true: there are zero images in this product at any layer -- no next/image, no img tag, and no poster, artwork, backdrop or thumbnail key anywhere in packages/contracts/src. Posters are CSS gradients.
assigned.notes: Acceptance reconciled in round 83 on gpt-architect's ruling after a round-83 audit found the original wording would have put a URL into the one contract whose header promises there is none, and would have stood a second artwork vocabulary beside the reviewed opaque-reference one in @liberty/catalog-ingestion. The reviewer ruled: do not claim under the old acceptance, preserve the opaque-reference architecture, and resolve the reference behind an authorized boundary. An architecture-review gate was added because the task now introduces a resolution boundary rather than a field.

recommended.title: Continue watching: resume where the viewer left off
recommended.acceptance: A viewer sees what they were watching and resumes it at the right position. The progress API, its lease route and its writer-epoch conflict rules are complete, tested and reviewed, and no rail, no card progress bar and no resume prompt exists. REQUIRED: a continue-watching rail on home, profile-scoped, ordered by recency, excluding finished items by a stated rule rather than a magic threshold buried in a component. REQUIRED: a progress indicator on cards for partially watched titles. REQUIRED: resume uses the stored position through the session's startAtSeconds, which the playback path already carries, rather than seeking after load -- the test matrix already lists 'resumed playback uses stored progress safely' as a regression scenario. REQUIRED: a viewer can start over; a resume that cannot be declined is a trap.
recommended.notes: PROPOSED FOR gpt-architect RULING, round 80. Created unowned as part of the WINDOWS PRODUCT COMPLETION phase board so the proposal is machine-readable rather than prose, and NOT claimed before the verdict.

recommended.title: Authentication entry and session UX
recommended.acceptance: A viewer who is signed out can do something about it. PW-0403 made a deployment answer 401 not_authenticated, and there is no screen anywhere in this application that consumes it: /api/auth/* is served and nothing links to it, so the honest description of a deployment today is that it refuses everybody correctly and offers them nowhere to go. REQUIRED: a sign-in screen reachable FROM the signed-out protected state, not only from a URL somebody knows. A 401 that renders as a generic error is the same dead end with better manners. REQUIRED: a sign-up flow where deployment policy permits it. Policy, not preference: requireEmailVerification and the absence of a mail transport both decide what can actually complete, and the screen must reflect what this deployment can do rather than what the library can. REQUIRED: a sign-out action, and an authenticated shell state -- the shell already carries the active profile badge from PW-0303, and who you are SIGNED IN AS is a different fact from which profile is selected. Both belong there and neither may be mistaken for the other. REQUIRED: a protected-view redirect or an equivalent actionable signed-out experience. Either is acceptable; what is not is a screen that silently renders empty because every request behind it returned 401. REQUIRED: verification and password-reset entry states. REQUIRED: EXPLICIT UX WHEN THE MAIL TRANSPORT IS UNAVAILABLE, and this is the clause most likely to be got wrong. The composition root's transport REJECTS rather than logging the link, because a verification or reset URL is a one-click account-takeover token; the screen must say the message cannot be sent and must NOT log, display, copy or otherwise expose such a token to work around it. A UI that showed the link to be helpful would undo the reason the placeholder throws. REQUIRED: it consumes /api/auth/* and does not invent a second auth protocol. No client-side session parsing, no second cookie, no parallel identity state -- the server is the authority and the screen reads its answers. REQUIRED: profile selection is NOT moved into Better Auth. Profiles live above auth (PL-0402), active_profile_selection stays keyed by session in Liberty's own store, and a sign-in screen is exactly where somebody would be tempted to fold the two together. REQUIRED: the server-side not_authenticated behaviour and the PW-0402 authorization boundaries are preserved. Nothing in this task may make a refusal more informative than it is today: the four session failure modes stay externally indistinguishable, and profile_unavailable keeps answering for both of its cases. MEASURED STARTING POINT: apps/web contains no sign-in, sign-up, sign-out or password-reset screen, no link to /api/auth anywhere, and exactly one client-side caller of this application's own API -- the profiles client PW-0303 introduced, whose rules this task should follow rather than re-derive.

recommended.title: Watchlist becomes usable: an add control and a list
recommended.acceptance: A person can add a title to their watchlist and see the list. The API and its mutation rules are complete, tested and reviewed -- including the conflict semantics in packages/persistence/src/watchlist-mutation.ts -- and nothing renders them. REQUIRED: the add control appears on the title screen and on a catalog card, and reflects state optimistically while remaining correct when the write is refused. REQUIRED: the resolution vocabulary the API already returns (accepted plus a reason, not a boolean ok) is surfaced honestly; a refused write must not render as a success, which is the shape of defect the harnesses in this repository have caught four times.

recommended.title: Offline, degraded and error states a desktop application needs
recommended.acceptance: The application behaves honestly when the network, the backend or the sidecar is unavailable. There is no offline handling of any kind today -- no navigator.onLine, no service worker, no offline banner, no retry-on-reconnect. THIS MATTERS MORE ON THE DESKTOP THAN IT DID ON THE WEB: docs/DESKTOP_PLAYBACK.md section 8 accepts that an offline desktop cannot resolve playback at all, and requires that failure be surfaced as an honest unavailable outcome rather than an empty candidate list -- so the UI half of that ruling is this task. REQUIRED: a network-state signal and a visible degraded mode that names what is unavailable. REQUIRED: recovery on reconnect without a manual reload. REQUIRED: the sidecar being down is a DISTINCT state from the backend being down and from the network being down, because the three have different remedies and collapsing them produces a support burden. REQUIRED: no state invents content; an offline home shows what it has and says so.
